```{r}
# What we do now that we know that there is spatial autocorrelation in the data 
# Moran's I
# weights matrix as inverse of distance
# calculate the euclidean distance and returns as a matrix object 
# divides one by every element 
w <- 1 / as.matrix(dist(st_coordinates(meuse)))
# solving for diagonial points 
diag(w) <- 0
# Rho-standardization - wighting the data
W <- mat2listw(w, style = "W")
# mat2list - takes the matrix and makes it a list 
moran.test(meuse$cadmium, mat2listw(w))
moran.test(residuals(cad_lm), mat2listw(w))
# We fit the model and we find that there is spatial autocorrelation amongst the variables 
# the errors are correlated with each other but not correlated with the errors of the dependent variable 
# Need to look at the p-value from the Rao's Score (Lagrange multipler)
# Compare the p-values between the error and the lag model - choose the one that is significant 
# If both are significant than you can test for a robust model - like you did with Jeff 

```

# a note on why we prefer lm.morantest rather than moran.test:
# moran.test is for testing spatial autocorrelation in primary variables
# it is inappropriate when applied to residuals of a model that includes
# covariates. It will produce the same result when applied to a model w/o
```{r}
# covariates: 
moran.test(meuse$cadmium, mat2listw(w))
lm.morantest(lm(cadmium~1, data=meuse), mat2listw(w))
tmp <- lm(cadmium~dist, data=meuse)
moran.test(tmp$residuals, mat2listw(w))
lm.morantest(tmp, mat2listw(w))
```


```{r}
# is there spatial autocorr in residuals of OLS model?
lm.morantest(cad_lm, mat2listw(w))
# is there something else in the model that I can use to explain the spatial autocorrelation 
# For us in Meuse, we are testing for spatial autocorrelation 
lm1 <- lm(cadmium ~ dist + ffreq, data=meuse)
lm.morantest(lm1, mat2listw(w))
meuse$cad_lm_resids <- lm1$residuals
plot(meuse["cad_lm_resids"])
```


```{r}
# weights matrix based on 8 nearest neighbors
# knn2nb - k nearest neighbors to neighbor best - subsetting for the 8 nearest neighbors 
w <- knn2nb(knearneigh(meuse, k=8))
lm.morantest(lm1, nb2listw(w))
```

```{r}
# weights matrix w/ varying number of neighbors, based off maximum nearest neighbor distance
nm <- knn2nb(knearneigh(meuse))
plot(nm, st_coordinates(meuse))
max_dist <- max(unlist(nbdists(nm, meuse)))
nb <- dnearneigh(meuse, 0, max_dist)
colW <- nb2listw(nb, style="W")
moran(meuse$cadmium, colW, length(nb), Szero(colW))
moran.test(meuse$cadmium, colW)
```

```{r}
# binary neighbor weights
colW <- nb2listw(nb, style="B")
?nb2listw
moran.test(meuse$cadmium, colW)
```

###################################################################
# Maybe don't pay attention here, but if you care, here's how to do GWR
###################################################################
```{r}
library(spgwr)
example(gwr)
optim_bw <- gwr.sel(cadmium~dist, data=meuse)
cad_gwr <- gwr(cadmium ~ dist, meuse, bandwidth = optim_bw, hatmatrix=TRUE)
# allows us to use the gwr to predict values at unmeasured points 
# important because the betas are different compared on your location 
cad_gwr_grid <- gwr(cadmium ~ dist, meuse, bandwidth = optim_bw, fit.points=meuse.grid, predict=T, fittedGWRobject=cad_gwr)
names(cad_gwr_grid)
names(cad_gwr_grid$SDF)
spplot(cad_gwr_grid$SDF, "pred")
spplot(cad_gwr_grid$SDF, "localR2")
spplot(cad_gwr_grid$SDF, "dist")
```

```{r}
# Spatial error
# Picking a spatial error model 
# We think that there is an ommitted spatial variable 
# Something providing spatial structure that we don't have in the model 
library(spatialreg)
# instead of lm we are going to use errorsarlm 
cad_selm <- errorsarlm(cadmium~dist, data=meuse, listw=colW)
cad_lm
lm.morantest(cad_selm, colW)
moran.test(cad_selm$resid, colW)
moran.test(cad_lm$resid, colW)
class(cad_selm)
lm.LMtests(residuals(cad_selm), colW)
# meuse$cad_selm_resids <- cad_selm$residuals
# moran.test(meuse$cad_selm_resids, colW)
```

qs <- quantile(meuse$cad_selm_resids, c(0, 0.02, 0.98, 1))
tmp_breaks <- seq(0, max(abs(qs[2:3])), len=5)
breaks <- c(-1 * max(abs(qs[c(1, 4)])), -1 * rev(tmp_breaks[2:length(tmp_breaks)]), tmp_breaks[2:length(tmp_breaks)], max(abs(qs[c(1, 4)])))
pal <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu"))
resid_cols <- pal(length(breaks) - 1)
plot(coordinates(meuse)[,1], coordinates(meuse)[,2], pch=16, cex=5, col=resid_cols[findInterval(meuse$cad_selm_resids, breaks, all.inside=T)])
legend("topleft", legend=paste(round(breaks, 1)[1:(length(breaks) - 1)], round(breaks, 1)[2:length(breaks)], sep="-"), pch=16, col=resid_cols, title="Cad. SEM Resids")

###################################################################
```{r}
# Spatial lag
# instead of errorsar we are using lagsar here
# dispersion process is inherent in the variable
cad_sllm <- lagsarlm(cadmium~dist, data=meuse, listw=colW)
# lm.morantest(cad_sllm, colW)
moran.test(cad_sllm$resid, colW)
moran.test(cad_lm$resid, colW)
```

lm.LMtests(residuals(cad_sllm), colW)
meuse$cad_sllm_resids <- cad_sllm$residuals
moran.test(meuse$cad_sllm_resids, colW)
summary(cad_sllm)

qs <- quantile(meuse$cad_sllm_resids, c(0, 0.02, 0.98, 1))
tmp_breaks <- seq(0, max(abs(qs[2:3])), len=5)
breaks <- c(-1 * max(abs(qs[c(1, 4)])), -1 * rev(tmp_breaks[2:length(tmp_breaks)]), tmp_breaks[2:length(tmp_breaks)], max(abs(qs[c(1, 4)])))
pal <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu"))
resid_cols <- pal(length(breaks) - 1)
plot(coordinates(meuse)[,1], coordinates(meuse)[,2], pch=16, cex=2,  col=resid_cols[findInterval(meuse$cad_sllm_resids, breaks, all.inside=T)])
legend("topleft", legend=paste(round(breaks, 1)[1:(length(breaks) - 1)], round(breaks, 1)[2:length(breaks)], sep="-"), pch=16, col=resid_cols, title="Cad. OLS Resids")

###################################################################
# Use the Lagrange multiplier test to help choose (read details in
# between lag, error, or SARMA models (read details in ?lm.LMtests)

```{r}
# make an inverse distance weighted matrix then
# turn it into a listw object:
w <- 1 / as.matrix(dist(st_coordinates(meuse))^2)
diag(w) <- 0
cad_listw <- mat2listw(w)
```

```{r}
# fit OLS model and perform Lagrange multiplier test to help
# select a spatial variant (if one is necessary)
# cad_lm <- lm(cadmium ~ dist, data = meuse)
cad_lm <- lm(log(cadmium) ~ dist, data = meuse)
lm.LMtests(cad_lm, cad_listw, test = "all")

plot(meuse$dist, log(meuse$cadmium))
```


# The lm.LMtests indicate that there is spatial autocorrelation in the OLS
# residuals that could be handled with a spatial error model (LMlag is not sig).
# Only one of LMerr and LMlag are significant, so we don't bother to look at the 
# robust variatns RLMerr and RLMlag, which would be unreliable unless both
# LMerr and LMlag are significant. If RLMerr and RLMlag also have sig p-values,
# then we choose the one with the higher test statistic (i.e. RLMerr or RLMlag value)
cad_selm <- errorsarlm(cadmium ~ dist, data=meuse, listw=cad_listw)
moran.test(cad_selm$residuals, listw=cad_listw)

# compare the estimated coefficients and their standard errors
# not only have we underestimated the std. error with the non-spatial
# version, our estimates are also slightly biased:
summary(cad_selm)
summary(cad_lm)

# why do we get a warning in lm.LMtests() above?
# It's because lm.LMtests() checks for a "style" attribute on the listw
# object that is not set by mat2listw, but is by nb2listw, for example.
# Straight from Roger B: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-geo/2007-November/002868.html
# "row standardization": https://support.esri.com/en/other-resources/gis-dictionary/term/d16e7467-f1a7-4cc0-ba18-74a5ef3ee19c
# compare with:
# cad_listwW <- nb2listw(cad_listw$neighbours, style="W")
# lm.LMtests(cad_lm, cad_listwW, test = "all")

```{r}
# This is a fairly common example using boston housing tract data
# the goal is to estimate the median home value within a tract based on
# tract-level covariates
data(boston)
boston_ols <- lm(log(MEDV) ~ CRIM + ZN + INDUS + CHAS + I(NOX^2) + I(RM^2) + AGE + log(DIS) + log(RAD) + TAX + PTRATIO + B + log(LSTAT), data=boston.c)
summary(boston_ols)
lm.morantest(boston_ols, nb2listw(boston.soi))
# The RStest stops when it hits the first significant p-value 
lm.RStests(boston_ols, nb2listw(boston.soi))
```
```{r}
data_dir <- "C:/Users/aasie/Downloads/spData-master/spData-master/data"
boston_tr <- st_read(file.path(data_dir, "boston/boston_tracts.shp"))
# you can get the shapefile here: https://github.com/Nowosad/spData/tree/master/inst/shapes
# boston_tr <- readShapePoly(system.file("etc/shapes/boston_tracts.shp", package="spdep")[1], ID="poltract", proj4string=CRS(paste("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD27 +no_defs +ellps=clrk66", "+nadgrids=@conus,@alaska,@ntv2_0.gsb,@ntv1_can.dat")))
plot(boston_tr)
# polygon to neighbor list 
# Rook definition - need to share at least two corner points to be neighbors
# Queen defintion - need to share at least one corner point to be a neighbor 
boston_nb <- poly2nb(boston_tr)
?poly2nb
boston_nb_rook <- poly2nb(boston_tr, queen=F)
```

# plot the tracts with their links
plot(boston_tr)
# plot(boston_nb, coordinates(boston_tr), add=T, pch=16, cex=0.5, col=2)
plot(boston_nb, coordinates(boston_tr), add=T, pch=16, cex=0.5, col=2)

# plot the "Rook's rule" version
plot(boston_tr)
plot(boston_nb_rook, coordinates(boston_tr), add=T, pch=16, cex=0.5, col=2)

```{r}
# inference from below model: select spatial error model
# both robust versions are sig, but the error model is much more sig
# and has a much higher error statistic
# Spirrously concluded with the linear model that additional variables would help when they actually would not 
lm.LMtests(boston_ols, nb2listw(boston_nb_rook), test = "all")
```

boston_spe <- errorsarlm(log(MEDV) ~ CRIM + ZN + INDUS + CHAS + I(NOX^2) + I(RM^2) + AGE + log(DIS) + log(RAD) + TAX + PTRATIO + B + log(LSTAT), data=boston.c, nb2listw(boston.soi))
lm.LMtests(residuals(boston_spe), nb2listw(boston.soi))

summary(boston_spe)
summary(boston_ols)
